data: Love this amazing game with great combat
it is really fun, very challenging and addictive
i love it is a very good game that has a good story
Incredible and diverse combat with an amazing soundtrack, plenty of replayability and an overall extremely polished and enjoyable game
Great story, beautiful graphics, and challenging
this game just feels like a chore, and there are way too many mechanics to keep track of
the game world, story and characters are mind-numbingly shallow and uninteresting
It just pushed all the wrong difficulty buttons and was such an unforgiving frustrating experience that I do not recommend anyone to play
Games should not feel like a slog, chore, or force hours of grinding just to progress to the next stage

One of my favorite souls like series. It's much easier than the first one, but the gameplay is still solid. The dub is passible, but that's not what you are here for. If you like hard soulslike games, definitely a pick up!

Better than Nioh 3 XD, but also suffers of the same repetitive enemies maximum 5 I've seen so far that keeps repeating and to make it worse, they are the worst op enemies as normal mobs. This game is just dumb overall. Tedious and repetitive, sub missions are the same copy pasted previous levels with the same mobs and ganks every direction.

I play tons of Souls-likes. I never really have trouble on any of them, Sekiro is one of my favorites games of all time. But there's something about the Nioh games that make make them crushingly difficult for me. So hard it's just not fun to play. Feels like you're meant to grind the obtuse loot system instead of mastering the combat itself.

A really fun game and an improvement over the first as a sequel should be. I took a lot more advantage of co-op this time around and it was very good as well as making some of the harder parts of the game more manageable. A lot of content and gameplay mechanics from the first game remain the same plus a ton of new additions. Unfortunately though that also includes performance issues, whenever the game loads a new area the game will stutter for a moment and it's noticeable but not as annoying as the first game when it would happen during fights and I would get killed. The game also crashed a handful of times which was frustrating, so because of those performance issues I can't recommend full price so make sure you get it on sale.

Coming from the Soulsborne games, this is my first "souls-like." I enjoyed it, but I felt like the story refused to end. That may not be a bad thing if you're loving every minute of it, but I was pretty ready to be done around 80% of the story. The combat does feel smooth, and I believe it would certainly reward deep diving and mastery. I wasn't into it for this play through, but if that's your thing, then you'll love this game.

Possibly the best combat out of any "souls like" game including any actual souls game. 

The build variety, character progression, loot system is S tier stuff. This is more like an action diablo / ARPG game than your typical souls like.

Best 20$ I've spent on a game.
Peak combat system with a lot of mechanics that you won't find in any other games.
Abilities and souls that makes you look cool ( that's why you should use em lol ).
Endless content with the dlcs and a bunch of bosses that are fun to counter.
Best co-op game I've ever played, even though it's not designed for that.
and since they're on sale rn you won't regret buying it, go for it.

Absolutely infuriatingly difficult and othersive immersive, fun experience.
Love that it has coop and many ways to play.

Take your time and learn the controls. It is difficult, very satisfying, and fluid. Play this game.
You dont need to know anything about the first. Their is a large player base, finding help is not difficult.
Worth it.
It's ok game but it's not for me. Everything feels very repetetive and all the time you have feeling like you didn't invest enought time to have fun. If you don't like grind do not play this game.

What a glow up. When you compare this to nioh 1, its absolutely crazy just how much Team Ninja improved. Wonderful soulslike with some awesomely aggressive and freeform combat, and a phenomenal soundtrack to boot. Still has a few issues in regards to loot management & some dull npc bosses, but definitely worth your time.
Challenging and rewarding, this is one of the only "soulslikes" (god I hate that term) that can actually be favourably compared to the FromSoft games.

Let me start by saying I am playing with a controller so I'm not effected by the mousey/keyboard hotkey prompts not showing issues.

I love/hate this game so much. The game play and core mechanics are very satisfying/infuriating.

I think I would love/hate the game even more if I was better/worse at it, as there are lots of different systems to master that continue to be unlocked after beating the main game on the regular difficulty. I'm just over 80 hours in and have started to dip into the equivalent of a New Game + mode, and will spend another 80+ hours on that.

The amount of content to gush/rage over in this game for the price is fantastic.

While not without it's issues, would recommend if you're a fan of the Dark Souls and/or the co-ops.
A fun, challenging and deep game. Kind of if Dark Souls had been built buy a fighting game company. Highly enjoyable if you don't mind a real learning curve.

10/10 For a hardcore player like me <3

It’s a brutally deep action RPG with top-tier combat, massive build variety, and challenging boss fights that feel insanely rewarding to beat. There’s a ton of content and replay value, so if you get hooked, it owns your time.

A masterpiece for players who love challenge and mastery…
and a headache for anyone just looking to relax.

Not generally into fast-paced, punishing games (couldn't get myself to stick with Bloodborne) but I'm enjoying Nioh 2 a lot. The level design and mission structure are great, providing a sense of direction and progress, and the different options for advancing and equipping your character give you lots of tactics to play with if you ever feel stuck. (Written as of reaching the second region in-game)
Also, the cosmetic character customization is great.

Here's my review for Nioh 2, now this is gonna be a little bit of a bias review cause I'm a Nioh 2 fanboy, I put a lot of hours into the PlayStation versions and now I'm at it again on PC, but lets get into it, it's probably one of the best action RPG games I've played in a long time and it still holds up well in this current gen of gaming as well.

There is a lot of depth and customization when it comes to the battle system, talents and character customizing overall, the game is mission based with a lot of neat and varying level designs, the boss battles are also pretty unique and full of depth.

Finally the only negative part of the game in my opinion is the story, it wasn't the best, if you're looking for a story game this one probably isn't it, but if you're looking for a game with in depth gameplay and mechanics definitely give it a try.

On an ending note the DLC for the game is also well put together with new levels, enemies, bosses and more, you won't be let down by it if you liked the base game content.

Overall my final score of the game is a 9.5/10, definitely give it a try if you're into souls likes or action RPG games.

Solid game play with a faster pace than Dark Soul.
Draw distance is a mess, some objects and shadows can pop in right in front of your eyes.

Nioh 2 is a masterclass in action RPG design, offering a challenging yet deeply rewarding experience that will keep players coming back for more. With its engaging combat, intricate level design, and richly detailed world, it stands as a shining example of the genre and a must-play title for fans of Japanese mythology and challenging gameplay alike.

Fighting system too complex, till it's not fun. The "Ki" pulse at the end of combos do what exactly?! Learning curve too steep. Encourages you to do more running then anything at this point because swings and blocks take too much stamina. To make matters worse: the quality of life, no jump, linear but maze-like boards aren't entertaining they're frustrating. I bought this game after the hurricane hit and only played it a few hours before not wanting to play it any further. Today I started out again with a fresh perspective but a few hours in and I'm back to being frustrated.
Brilliant game with lots of replayability. Still didn't end up "finishing" the game after 160 hours. Well worth your time.

I wish I knew how ridiculously grindy and unbalanced the game becomes in the later runs. Unironically, the first play-through has more freedom for builds because everything is viable unlike later difficulties where the game forces you to play in a very specific way because of the absurd enemy hp, stamina and damage numbers. Overall, it's a 7/10 game, maybe an 8/10 if I rate it based on just the first run.

Extremely fun game, I was never able to get into the first game and didn't know why. This game taught me to quit going at it like a Souls game and it instantly became 100x more fun. Lots of missions, lots of weapons, combat is difficult but fair. Other games go for artificial difficulty where they ramp the bullshit up by a million while nerfing your character into oblivion. In this game if you master the basics you're set, and any difficulty feels genuine rather than artificial and forced. Enemies constantly drop items, grinding in this game is nowhere near as much of a chore as it is in other games such as the Souls games. Definitely a 10/10 game in my opinion, absolutely worth a play
Koei Tecmo did a wonderful job by making Wo Long absolutely unplayable in both single, coop so that players go back to nioh 2 .. amazing marketing plan
I enjoyed this game alot however on PC I died more to the janky camera views than anything. I've never stopped playing a game for terrible camera but this was a deal-breaker for me.

Get a friend, go ham.
Game is a much better co-op experience in comparison to the traditional soulsborne.

My absolute favourite game in the "souls like" genere

if you ever wondered "what would be like if my souls character didnt swing their weapon like a idiot?" (looking at you dark souls) well now you can,you fight like a souls boss
You can pull off some crazy combos almost dmc style and transform yourself into bosses/enemies mid combos for some crazy mixups,highly recommended if you want a souls like with faster paced combat
eagerly waiting for a nioh 3

Best ARPG in recent years, taking the first game`s formula wich was pretty cool integrating fast Ninga Gaiden-ish combat with Diablo-esque loot and a Souls-like "bonfire" resting place/reset system but also improving the formula, changing Living Weapon`s "nuke all" button to Yokai Shift wich adds many mobility, utility and differs between the 3 types, also Cores were a very cool new addition and the best weapon type has been added, fists.

Not a game for all by any means but the way this game beats you down at first but at late game you can also become all mighty and stomp whoever stomped you before is so satisfying, and for me its Goty 2021.

Bad designed wannabe git gud game. If the game is so hard because the controlls are clunky, then it's just a bad game. If a mob needs just 2 hits for me but I need 7 trillion hits, then it's just bad game design. If armor doesn't matter because you get 2 shoted naked but also get 2 shoted with 7 gezillion armor, then it's bad game design. If adding hp doesn't matter because you get 2 shoted anyway, then it's bad game design. If you can't lower the difficulty to enjoy the game you've spend money on, then it's bad game design. If you need to read/watch 25 guides because the game is too hard and there is no way to get better, then it's bad game design.

Story: Mid to Low (4/10)
Gameplay: Very Good to Excellent (9/10).

TLDR; Gameplay wise it is better than any souls like game (except Sekiro?), the story is just some extra side dish.

An absolute blast to play. Ruthless, punishing, and requires you to think of every approach possible to gain the upper hand. Nothing beats the satisfaction of overcoming difficulties, and Nioh 2 brings that satisfaction to you in a beautiful, historical Japanese package.
Really good game with a large amount of NG+ cycles that keep making the game better. Highly recommend

Nioh 2 is a great buy and you can definitely have a good time playing it first, but I would recommend Nioh 1 more.

Many improvements have been made to the sequel. There are a few new weapons that feel unique. the biggest additions to combat are transformations and special moves, that are really cool. Both compete for the same resource that takes a while to build up. You can only use them rarely so it usually feels exactly like Nioh 1 (which is still the best combat system ever). Nioh 2 does add a lot of enemies and bosses which is fantastic, the multiplayer mechanic is improved and there is a nice npc ally system.

Both games are a 10/10. Nioh 1 wins mostly for its sale price, it's a very big game for a very low price. if thats not a problem, nioh 2 is just as good to start with.

The beginning of both games are a bit drab because it has to teach you how to play, and there's a lot to teach. Both games are quite difficult and demanding which might be a deal-breaker depending on your taste.

I originally played an hour and refunded thinking this game was too overwhelming. After trying to find a new game that met my specific criteria: custom character creation, diablo-style loot, and personalized play-styles, I came across this game again and decided to give it a second try. I'm very happy that I did.

Once you wrap your head around the array of combat and RPG mechanics the game really clicks. It's not as complicated as it initially seems, and a lot of mechanics are there just in case you want the extra options, rather than the game forcing you to use all the mechanics constantly.

There is no question this game is difficult and punishing, but there are numerous systems that help out. Things like yokai form, ranged, blocking, or farming a level or two can really open the game up if you're struggling. Defeating a truly difficult boss with your personal combat style and seeing the rain of colored loot is unmatched by any souls-like or ARPG.

Highly recommended for people who enjoy mastering combat systems, looting, and character building.

A true Sequel, it fixes most of what was wrong with Nioh 1 (a good game already IMO) and adds so much more, while people who hated Nioh 1 wont enjoy this Game either, if you fell of of Nioh 1 due to its Endgame i suggest giving this one a try.
The port is okay, it runs in up to 120 fps (no 144 fps) and has a lack of Graphics Options, So far it crashed once for me but otherwise runs perfectly at 60 fps on my 1060 6gb. I havent encountered any Bugs or Glitches so far and am overall very happy with the game.

Gameplay is very similar to Nioh 1 except it adds new mechanics to spice things up and gives you your own character to play as. It's one of those perfect sequels. Some frame rate issues here and there when a lot is going on but resolved after altering settings kept that issue under control. Enjoy the game!
About as bad as the first game. Zero balance, zero fairness. These devs do not know how to do anything other than artificial difficulty.

One of the best souls likes out there. I call it high speed dark souls with numbers. Very technical, lots of menus and cool systems that can be overwhelming at first but once youre comfortable this is one of the best gameplay experiences with loads of personalization and different ways to play. I cant recommend it highly enough. I almost 100% the first game and then pre ordered the steel case special edition on playstation and DID 100% this one. Rebought on PC to show the way to some friends. Theyre in love also.

This game is an epitome of every bad design choice you could make while trying to copy From Software games. It's just too bloated. Too many artificial mechanics to keep track of against cheap hitting enemies with wild movements and bad telegraphs that will kill you in one combo and have absurd amount of hp. This is complete opposite of Dark Souls, Sekiro or Elden Ring design - tightly designed and consistent systems where you know what you can expect from enemies and know what are your possibilities and there is a general feel of fairness. This is Feature Creep the game that is constantly trying to be more unfair than the previous bit.

And then they further killed it by atrocious generic random loot system that renders your weapon useless sooner than you can level it up.

Environments are dull and uninspired, often repeating.

EDIT: After realizing that this is not really a souls like game and has features that are not in tandem with my preferences I change my rating to recommend, because it sure is a quality game for people who enjoy this type of experience.

Game is more then excellent!
I have invest over 1350h on PS4 and am more then glad to invest even more on PC version!
Port is very nicely done comparing to Nioh 1! All recommendations 10/10!
There are certain tweaking that shall be done but overall it's great!
Currently anywhere outside there is no better Action RPG Combat game then Nioh, complexity, combat deepness, variety.
P.S. My gameplay and hours speaks more then I can write or say here!

Do you like challenging but fair game play?

Do you like build diversity? Skill trees? Skill customization? Do you enjoy min-maxing and fine tuning builds? Do you like equipment stats? Oh god, the sheer bulk of the different stats and set effects.

Do you like hard games that give you near limitless options to take on fights? Games with so many ways to approach combat encounters that even cheesing through a fight feels like you are being rewarded for your creativity? Do you like that? Huh? Do you?

Dose Dark Souls crossed with a Fighting Game sound fun to you?

Do you know what God Hand is? Did you like God Hand's customizable combo system? (No? Fuck you then.)

Are you and 1-2 other people looking for a fun and challenging game to co-op together?

Do you like New game +? New game ++ ? New game +++? New ga- ...You get the idea.
...Or maybe you don't and in that case: This game has a lot of new game +'s and each one adds new content and increases the difficulty of missions and bosses.

If you said "yes" to at least three of these, then you will like Nioh 2.

If you said "yes" to all of these then you will think that Nioh 2 is one of the greatest games ever made.

"Nioh 2 is a phenomenal combat masterpiece! Its loop is addicting as hell, blending technical stances with wild Yokai powers. Replaying is a blast, as NG+ refreshes the challenge with new enemy placements and surprising new attacks for regular foes. It’s a rewarding, endless demon-slaying party. Highly recommended!"

diffcult game - checked
loot based - checked

If dark souls and diablo have a baby - this is it

Unique Soulslike with some twist

One of soulslike that throw some wrench on soulslike formula, the combat stance system really improve the gameplay, also the pvp revenant system is really good (legit I can feel playing PVP without need fighting the real human lmao), no open world but using mission system, but it's really good since you don't need figure out how to start again

+ Unique Stance system
+ Weapon type is so many, you can choose which one you like
+ Yokai and Art is really good
+ Skill Customization, some moveset you can modify it

- No Unique Weapon Art so every wep bit generic, only differ in models
(correction, there is some boss skills that can be dropped from some certain boss)
- Story is not that strong, still good tho
- Stamina management is bit ass if you don't use the Ki Mechanic

oh also while in steam deck compability is playable, it's fully compatible with the steam deck, there is some hiccup on some stage, but I can manage since it's 30-40 fps, you can lock it to 30 fps if you want
It's fine if you like Souls, but its also bloated with a lot of stuff. I prefer simplicity. I'd give it a 3.5 out of 5.

Nioh 2 is a fast paced souls-like game that keeps you on the edge.
It is very fun with co-op or alone.
Highly recommended
Had a blast with it! Finished the base game through co op with no issues, story line could be better imo. I AM SO HYPED FOR NG+!!!!

Same as Nioh 1, but with more stuff. More abilities, more ultimate modes, more weapons. It has a great character creator.

If you like 1, you will like 2.

Nioh 2 is an attractive game with excellent combat, and a bewildering number of options on how to refine your build to create your specifically preferred style of combatant. That is the entire draw. The narrative is nonsense. The levels are tight and lousy with reused assets. I came to Nioh 2 thinking of it as a Souls-like, but it is definitely its own thing. Nioh 2 has better combat, but comparatively little level exploration and no sense of awe-striking environmental scale.

Great game. There is a lot of content, the fights are fast paced, good enemy variety and in my opinion the best part of the game is all the different weapons and builds you can try. You can find a style that works for you.

The story can feel lacking, especially since your character doesn't talk and just seems to get caught up in events. Also, there is too much gear, you get a set of armor and it is usually irrelevant after the next mission. This is less true later on but at least through your first play through of the game.

Overall, this is a lot of fun and highly recommended.

tldr.text: Very Positive (90%): players mostly praise the combat.
The most common complaint is that the gameplay can feel like a chore.

details.text: Recent reviews are a little less positive, at 85%, so buyers today still find a well-liked game.
New players are less convinced, while players with over 50 hours are far more positive.
